notice: GTT Method Plans (methodology profiles). The human SELECTS a plan; the CLI records it (gtt-project.sh profile set); what Light, Medium, Hard and Team MEAN is defined here, by the Bootstrap, and nowhere else. A plan is an operating and collaboration profile - how much deterministic work the human delegates to GTT - never a quality level. Each rule says where it is enforced: `gates` are machine-enforced by the deterministic checks; `semantics` and `relaxes` are consumed by agents through the bootstrap skill and AGENTS.md (instruction plane); `plan.policy` is declared here and executed by the CLI (the Bootstrap does not re-implement it). No plan weakens an invariant. Human-readable rendering: .gtt/docs/method-plans.md.

selection.statement: The plan is the human's choice. The Bootstrap asks for it and never infers one silently - not from the project, not from the ADE, not from a previous project.
selection.asks_for: methodological intent (one of the four plans), never the technical policies derived from it

unselected.reason: `default` is only the gate fallback of a project where no plan has been selected yet (the behaviour before plans existed). It is never a selection, is always reported as `not selected`, and does not excuse the Bootstrap from asking.

selection.change: A plan can be selected or changed later without recreating the project: only .gtt/methodology.json is written; governed context, ADRs, proposals, backlog, index and history are untouched.

after_freeze: Selecting a LESS strict plan in a frozen project is refused: it is a governed change (change request -> proposal -> human decision). Selecting a stricter one is allowed.

definitions.deterministic_operation: An operation whose result follows entirely from repository state and declared policy, with no judgment: allocating the next free id, rebuilding the index, regenerating the GTTGuard registry, running validation.
definitions.relevant_change: An automated operation that rewrites human-authored or ADE-facing files rather than derived ones: updating references across documents after a move, synchronising ADE context files.
definitions.destructive_operation: An operation that removes or overwrites something that cannot be regenerated: clean, removing an ADE, overwriting a file.
definitions.governed_decision: Anything that changes L0/L1 (gtt-domain/context/, gtt-domain/adr/), the structure of the backlog, a GTTGuard-protected artifact, or the freeze. Always a human decision, in every plan.

policy_values.automatic: GTT does it without asking and reports what it did.
policy_values.automatic_safe: GTT does it without asking only when nothing human-authored would be overwritten; otherwise it stops and asks.
policy_values.confirm: GTT prepares the change, shows it, and applies it after the human confirms.
policy_values.propose_confirm: GTT proposes the value or change with its reasoning; nothing is reserved or written until the human confirms.
policy_values.team_policy: As the team declares in gtt-domain/working-agreements.md; where the team has declared nothing, `propose_confirm` applies.
policy_values.required: Always needs an explicit human confirmation.
policy_values.not_required: No separate confirmation; the operation is reported.
policy_values.recommended: Expected; its absence is reported, never a failure.
policy_values.possible: Supported; the plan is not designed around it.
policy_values.central: The plan is designed around it.
policy_values.standard: Every governed change is traceable through its proposal, ADR and promotion script.
policy_values.reinforced: Standard traceability plus the acting person recorded for each governed change and its review.

developer_experience.principle: The developer decides what only the developer can decide. GTT does everything else. Lower friction never means less governance: nothing here weakens an invariant, a gate or a human confirmation the selected plan requires.
developer_experience.applies_to: The rule is one; its effect differs by plan. What GTT does without asking and what it asks for is derived from the selected plan's `plan.policy` and returned as `interaction` by methodology.profile.get: Light asks only for governed decisions and destructive operations; Medium also confirms relevant changes; Hard also proposes ids for confirmation; Team follows the team's declared policy. Nothing is asked twice and nothing a plan requires is skipped.

decision_rule.statement: Before asking the human anything, determine whether the answer already follows objectively from the sources below. If it does, act, validate the result and continue. If it does not, name the decision, explain it briefly and ask once.
resolve_from: the actual state of the project
never_ask: whether to find another id when one is occupied
whether to update references the plan makes automatic
whether to continue to the next planned task after a successful step
for a policy the plan or a working agreement already defines

automatic_operations.what: the next free id when the requested one is occupied
automatic_operations.note: returns the id with `resolution`: `use` under a plan whose identity_resolution is automatic (Light, Medium), `propose` otherwise (Hard, Team) - the human then confirms it when reviewing the package

automatic_operations.what: GTTGuard registry sync, index rebuild and validation after any operation
automatic_operations.note: under a plan whose reference_updates is automatic (Light) it also reconciles unambiguous moves; under the others it stops with the exact command

protected_operations.statement: An operation on a governed or protected artifact that needs human authorization (approve, promote, advance a governed stage, copy, move, delete, overwrite, modify) is never reconstructed by hand: GTT provides one directly executable script that contains the complete operation, checks its preconditions, fails explicitly when the expected state is absent, and is safe to run from the project root. The agent prepares it and gives the one-line command; the human runs it; GTT then validates the result and continues.

stop_conditions: a genuine architectural or semantic conflict
a decision only the developer can make
explicit authorization required for a protected or governed operation
a safety or integrity condition that prevents continuing safely
unresolved evidence that is required to continue correctly
developer_experience.stop_rule: STOP is not a general precaution. Reaching an intermediate mechanical step is never a reason to stop.
developer_experience.continuity: After a successful automatic operation, continue the planned workflow and say so in one line; do not ask whether to continue.

contains: whether the developer must act, with the exact command
report.detail_on_demand: Detail is always available and never withheld: the `--verbose` form of an operation, `status`, `query`, and the full output of any check.

invariants.statement: Agents prepare; only a human decides, ratifies and freezes. No profile, ADE or Primary ADE changes that.
[PROPUESTA] never appears inside governed context; [FUENTE], [VACIO] and [CONFLICTO] must be well formed wherever they are used.
Sources -> grounding -> evidence dossier -> reasoning -> proposal -> human decision. Reasoning does not receive raw sources in a way that bypasses grounding.
A proposal is never a decision and is never written as one.
A conflict between sources is exposed, never silently resolved; an unresolved [CONFLICTO] refuses freeze.
An OPEN gap is scoped, visible and authorises nothing; a BLOCKING gap refuses freeze.
Freeze is a human ratification; there is no unfreeze shortcut. A frozen L0/L1 is changed only through the governed path.
GTTGuard-protected artifacts and the frozen governed context are never modified autonomously.
A selected source is not a governed authority; authority and precedence are declared, never inferred.

plan.label: Light Method
plan.summary: Maximum safe automation and the fewest interruptions, for one developer or a governed prototype.
plan.delegates: Every deterministic operation and every relevant change that is safe. You are asked only for governed decisions and destructive operations.

semantics.proposal_rigor: A proposal may be a short note in gtt-domain/proposals/; alternatives and risk may be one line each.
semantics.confirmation_requirements: Confirmation A (source) and Confirmation B (context) stay explicit and separate, but may be requested in the same interaction.
semantics.documentation_depth: solution-vision, stack and constraints are enough to freeze; architecture, principles and glossary may stay minimal.
semantics.adr_expectations: An ADR is expected only for a structural change to what is already frozen.
semantics.change_process: Change request is required for governed context; routine implementation needs none.
semantics.validation_gates: gtt-validate.sh; provenance policy advisory; warnings do not block freeze.
semantics.freeze_expectations: Freeze when the context is real and no BLOCKING gap or unresolved conflict remains.
semantics.audit_requirements: None scheduled; run gtt-audit on demand.
semantics.promotion_rigor: Human reviews the promotion script output before running it.
semantics.evidence_requirements: Record what was run only when a claim about it is made.

relaxes.how: Only solution-vision, stack and constraints must be non-template before freeze; the other three files may stay minimal but must not contain template placeholders.
No ADR for changes that do not alter frozen governed context.
Confirmation A and B may be asked in one exchange; each still needs its own explicit human answer.

plan.label: Medium Method
plan.summary: Automation with confirmation of relevant changes, for an individual project or a small team.
plan.delegates: Every deterministic operation. You confirm relevant changes before they are applied, as well as governed decisions and destructive operations.

intended_for: individual projects or small teams that want to confirm relevant changes

semantics.proposal_rigor: Full proposal: current decision, requested change, reason, impact, risk, alternatives.
semantics.confirmation_requirements: Confirmation A and B, each explicit and separate.
semantics.documentation_depth: All six governed context files real (no template text) before freeze.
semantics.adr_expectations: An ADR for every architectural decision that changes governed context.
semantics.change_process: Change request -> proposal -> human decision -> promotion package -> human execution.
semantics.validation_gates: gtt-validate.sh including provenance (advisory), integrity and stack checks.
semantics.freeze_expectations: Freeze after both confirmations; BLOCKING gaps and unresolved conflicts resolved; OPEN gaps scoped.
semantics.audit_requirements: gtt-audit before a release or after a large merge.
semantics.promotion_rigor: Promotion package: ADR draft, full affected context, human-run script with diffs.
semantics.evidence_requirements: Verification claims are classified (STATIC / RUNTIME VERIFIED, DOCUMENTED ONLY, NO EVIDENCE) when recorded.

plan.label: Hard Method
plan.summary: Explicit human authorization of every governed operation, for production and critical systems.
plan.delegates: Derived state only (index, validation). Ids and relevant changes are proposed and wait for your confirmation. Hard is explicit control, not manual work.

semantics.proposal_rigor: Full proposal with explicit alternatives, rollback and blast radius; no promotion from an informal note.
semantics.confirmation_requirements: Confirmation A and B, each explicit and separate, recorded in gtt-completion.md.
semantics.documentation_depth: All six governed context files real, every technology row cited ([FUENTE] or a Locked-by ADR), a source manifest declared.
semantics.adr_expectations: An ADR for every change to governed context, including small ones; the stack map delta is exact.
semantics.change_process: Change request -> analysis -> proposal -> human decision -> promotion package -> human execution -> validation; no shortcuts.
semantics.validation_gates: gtt-validate.sh with provenance policy required; warnings block freeze.
semantics.freeze_expectations: Freeze only with a source manifest, every OPEN gap scoped and carrying `affects`, no BLOCKING gap, no unresolved conflict, no warning.
semantics.audit_requirements: gtt-audit before every promotion and on a schedule.
semantics.promotion_rigor: Promotion script reviewed by a second person where the team has one; hashes verified before and after.
semantics.evidence_requirements: Every verification claim recorded with command, result and evidence type; NO EVIDENCE stated for what was not run.

plan.label: Team Method
plan.summary: Collaborative governance: the Hard gates plus CI, actor traceability and shared team policy.
plan.delegates: What the team declares in gtt-domain/working-agreements.md. Until the team declares it, ids and relevant changes are proposed and wait for confirmation, as in Hard.
plan.maturity_note: Today Team is the Hard gates plus the collaboration requirements below. Dedicated team plans are planned and will refine this definition; until they ship, nothing beyond what is written here is promised.

intended_for: several people or several ADEs changing the same governed project

semantics.proposal_rigor: Full proposal with explicit alternatives, rollback and blast radius, naming its author; no promotion from an informal note.
semantics.confirmation_requirements: Confirmation A and B, each explicit and separate, recorded in gtt-completion.md with the person who gave it.
semantics.documentation_depth: All six governed context files real, every technology row cited ([FUENTE] or a Locked-by ADR), a source manifest declared.
semantics.adr_expectations: An ADR for every change to governed context, including small ones, naming who decided; the stack map delta is exact.
semantics.change_process: Change request -> analysis -> proposal -> review by a second person -> human decision -> promotion package -> human execution -> validation in CI; no shortcuts.
semantics.validation_gates: gtt-validate.sh with provenance policy required, run in CI on every change; warnings block freeze.
semantics.freeze_expectations: Freeze only with a source manifest, every OPEN gap scoped and carrying `affects`, no BLOCKING gap, no unresolved conflict, no warning, and the CI gate configured.
semantics.audit_requirements: gtt-audit before every promotion and on a schedule the team declares in gtt-domain/working-agreements.md.
semantics.promotion_rigor: Promotion script reviewed by a second person and run by a person other than its author where the team allows it; hashes verified before and after; the base revision checked so a concurrent change is detected, never overwritten.
semantics.evidence_requirements: Every verification claim recorded with command, result, evidence type and who ran it; NO EVIDENCE stated for what was not run.
